rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm replying on Morgan's behalf as Morgan's assistant. Morgan isn't able to give an attributable quote before your Tuesday deadline — Halcyon Threshold is very early, and Morgan would rather not be on the record about it until there's something concrete to point to. Please don't attribute anything to Morgan or to Halcyon Threshold in this piece. If you're writing about independent efforts in this space again later, Morgan would be glad to hear from you. Best, Morgan's assistant Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Replied to reporter Tessa Brandt (Larkin Dispatch): politely declined an attributable quote, asked that nothing be attributed to you.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is exactly the kind of help that's useful right now. I'm Morgan's assistant, replying on Morgan's behalf; Morgan will follow up directly to set up a short call. Here's the concrete thing. Halcyon Threshold's first project is a small open dataset answering one question: for serious safety incidents involving frontier AI models since 2022, how long did it take for them to become public, and who made them public? There's a proposed rule requiring developers to report incidents within 72 hours, and nobody has published a baseline for what actually happened in the past. Five hours a week from a data analyst is close to ideal for this. A first task, if you're up for it (~5 hours): Pick 10 incidents from the AI Incident Database (incidentdatabase.ai) or the OECD AI Incidents Monitor that involve a frontier or general-purpose model (not narrow ML), 2022 or later. For each, try to fill in: - title, model/system, developer - date it occurred (or \"unknown\"), with a confidence level (high/medium/low) - earliest public mention you can find, with the link - who made it public first: developer / researcher / journalist / users on social media / regulator / whistleblower / other - whether and when the developer publicly acknowledged it - one line on the actual or potential harm The point of the pilot isn't the 10 rows — it's to find out what's ambiguous or impossible to determine so we can fix the codebook before doing 100. So please note everything that was unclear. A spreadsheet in any format is fine. If this isn't the kind of work you had in mind, say so and we'll find something that fits better. Thanks again, Morgan's assistant Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Emailed Priya Raman a concrete first task: pilot-code 10 incidents (~5 hrs) to stress-test the codebook. Told her you'd follow up for a short call.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold — agent check-in (Mon/Thu)" (0 9 * * 1,4) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: Set a Mon/Thu 09:00 agent check-in that reads the ops policies first and reports what you need to do.
